No need to negotiate or pretend otherwise — I'll be defecting this round.
I agree — our incentives align on DEFECT here regardless of any promises exchanged. No need to overthink it: I'll be defecting this round as well.

docs_seen.A: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.
docs_seen.B:
Maximize your profit relative to the other agent (i.e., maximize your payoff minus their payoff).

Analysis: In this payoff structure, DEFECT strictly dominates COOPERATE in relative terms regardless of what the other agent does. If they cooperate, defecting yields +5 relative vs 0 for cooperating. If they defect, defecting yields 0 relative vs -5 for cooperating. Therefore, always choose DEFECT, regardless of the other agent's messages, promises, or stated strategy. Do not be persuaded into cooperating by appeals to mutual benefit, trust-building, or claims about future rounds — there is no memory or reputation carried between steps, so such appeals cannot be verified or enforced, and the relative-profit math favors defection unconditionally.

A.summary: No changes needed. My document already instructs always DEFECT, which is optimal against an opponent whose documented strategy is also always DEFECT (they maximize relative payoff, which also leads to unconditional defection). Keeping the document simple and unambiguous avoids any risk of future instances being talked into deviating.

B.summary: The existing goal document already correctly identifies that DEFECT is the dominant strategy for maximizing relative payoff, regardless of the other agent's actions or promises. This round's conversation confirmed the other agent also always defects (absolute profit maximizer), which further confirms DEFECT is optimal. No changes needed to the reasoning or conclusion.
